clue.text: Correspondent fed back through the vital E region

indicators.note: something fed back is returned, so the letters picked up are read in the opposite direction
the answer runs through the words that follow, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A journalist sends a report back from some critical region labelled E.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through' marks letters hidden in 'thE VITAL E Region', giving EVITALER; 'fed back' turns them round. 'Correspondent' looks like a reporter but is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Relative and correspondent both mean matching or proportionate to something else, as in 'pay relative to effort'.

clue.text: End-user's unrefined vulgarity

indicators.note: unrefined means crude and unprocessed, so the letters of the fodder are rearranged rather than left in order

parts.note: end-user with its possessive S gives eight letters, all used

explanation.surface: The consumer at the end of the line is coarse and vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the 'S of 'End-user's' is part of the fodder: ENDUSERS, rearranged under 'unrefined', gives the two-word answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse bad manners are a kind of vulgarity; the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Time until one departs?

parts.note: reads like the span of a natural lifetime, but 'time' is prison time served until the inmate leaves

explanation.definitionFit: A prison term that lasts until the convict dies or is released, since 'time' is slang for a jail term.

clue.text: Obsessive tourist clocking up Iberia air-miles on part-exchange?

indicators.note: a partial exchange swaps only the opening parts of two words, which is how a Spoonerism trades their starts

parts.note: Iberia is the peninsula, here standing for Spain
a trotter, as in globetrotter, is someone racking up travel miles

explanation.surface: A keen traveller trades in airline loyalty points earned flying to Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tourist clocking up Iberia air-miles' describes a SPAIN TROTTER; swapping the opening SP and TR under 'on part-exchange' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail enthusiast who logs locomotive numbers is the stock example of a hobbyist with an obsession.

clue.text: Comedienne's plum deal?

parts.note: the Victoria is a popular variety of plum
deal is softwood timber such as pine or fir

explanation.surface: A comic's joke about a lucrative contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plum deal' reads as a cushy contract, but each word is a separate piece: a plum variety and a timber.
explanation.definitionFit: The late British comic and writer famous for sketches and stand-up was a celebrated female comedian.

clue.text: Rare result after five days leaving you dreadfully destitute

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests things in a terrible mess, so the remaining letters are jumbled
leaving means a letter departs from the word destitute before the rest is used

parts.note: U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: Someone is left penniless after a rare outcome at the end of five long days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' drops U from DESTITUTE to give DESTITTE, which 'dreadfully' rearranges. A five-day Test match in cricket very rarely ends level on runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket Test played over five days almost never finishes with both sides on equal runs, so such an outcome is a rarity.

clue.text: Did upset rank certainty pushing through, photo evidence shows

indicators.note: pushing through means the jumbled letters force their way into the middle of the other word
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word did is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the word did, which reads the same either way

indicators.note: rank means rotten or foul, so the word certainty is spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A certainty that ranks high forces its way through, as the photographs show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the palindrome DID round, leaving it unchanged; 'rank' (rotten) is the anagram signal, and 'pushing through' sets the jumbled letters inside. 'shows' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ID with a photograph on it is the standard document people show as proof of who they are.

clue.text: United's distribution's useless, cutting efficiency "in the engine room"

indicators.note: distribution spreads things around, so the letters of United are dealt out in a fresh order

parts.note: the word United, with the possessive adding no letter
NG is short for no good

explanation.surface: A football club's passing is poor, hurting its efficiency in midfield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distribution' rearranges UNITED into DETUNI; then add NG. The engine-room quote suggests a team's midfield, but it is an actual engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjusting an engine away from its optimum tuning lowers its performance, which is reducing its efficiency.

clue.text: Volte-face by Miliband's intended opposition

indicators.note: a volte-face is an about-turn, so the name that follows is turned back to front

parts.note: Ed Miliband, former leader of the UK Labour Party
one's intended is the person one is engaged to marry

explanation.surface: A politician's partner does a sudden U-turn against him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volte-face' reverses ED (Miliband's first name) to DE, followed by FIANCE. Ed Miliband led Britain's Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Open resistance to authority is a form of opposition.

clue.text: Often shift work, when knocking off early, can work round Britain

indicators.note: round means going all around, so the two pieces enclose the letter for Britain
to knock off early is to stop before the end, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: john and can are both slang for a toilet
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone working shifts finishes early and tours Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is slang for a toilet, not a tin; 'when' is a link. The first 'work' belongs to the definition, the second to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps moving from one post to another frequently changes employment.

clue.text: See 5
Acquire the heart of a Vulcan on return journey

indicators.note: a return journey heads back the way it came, so the kept letters are read backwards
the heart is the middle, so only the central letters of the name are kept

parts.note: Mr Spock of Star Trek is the best-known Vulcan

explanation.surface: Picking up the core of a spaceship on its trip home.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vulcan is Spock from Star Trek; 'the heart of' leaves POC, and 'on return journey' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cop is slang for to get or catch, as in 'cop a look', so it means obtaining something.

clue.text: Crown, Cow, Dog & Fox all have one play area

definitions.text: Crown, Cow, Dog & Fox all have one
definitions.meaning: each of these pub names has a ring-shaped letter at its exact middle
the ring marked at the middle of a football pitch, where play starts

explanation.surface: Four pubs each have their own playground.
explanation.definitionFit: Each name's middle letter is a ring, and a football pitch has a ring marked at halfway for kick-offs.

clue.text: Sun getting involved with Operation Meddle?

indicators.note: getting involved means becoming mixed up, so the two words' letters mingle into a new order

explanation.surface: A tabloid paper gets mixed up in a military operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting involved' mixes SUN and OPERATION; 'with' is a link. The tabloid Sun is a natural misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: To interfere uninvited in others' affairs is the idiom of sticking a rowing blade into their boat.

clue.text: I may get depressed if you want to get off again in the morning

definitions.text: I may get depressed if you want to get off again in the morning

parts.words: I may get depressed if you want to get off again in the morning
parts.note: reads as a gloomy speaker, but 'depressed' means pressed down, and 'get off' means fall back asleep

explanation.definitionFit: The alarm clock key pressed for a few more minutes' sleep before rising.

clue.text: Help notes

definitions.meaning: the international distress call asking for rescue
plural of so, the fifth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.definitionFit: A distress signal is a plea for rescue, and in tonic sol-fa 'so' is a note, so several are a set of notes.

clue.text: Determined to succeed as baby

indicators.note: to succeed is to follow on, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: cos is a casual short form of because, which as can mean
set means fixed or determined, as in a set price

explanation.surface: A child is determined to get on in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baby' is the verb here, to pamper, not a noun; 'to succeed' places the second piece after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To pamper or spoil someone is to treat them indulgently, which is what babying them means.

clue.text: Silver-spoon-weaned triplets onto purees

indicators.note: to puree is to mash into pulp, so the letters of the two words are mashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Babies from a rich family are fed pureed food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purees' is a verb here, mashing TRIPLETS and ONTO together.
explanation.definitionFit: A child born with a silver spoon in its mouth is raised in privilege and over-indulged.

clue.text: Kept one's cards close to be just good enough for raised stakes

indicators.note: stakes as a verb means to fence in with posts, so the outer pieces enclose the inner one

parts.note: to close is to stop

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means lifted upward, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to do is to suffice, as in 'that will do'
at and to both indicate a destination, as in 'arrive at'

explanation.surface: A poker player played their hand close to the chest, enough for the higher stakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses the short verb, and 'stakes' (fences in) has the outer pair enclose it. In poker, to stand pat is to keep one's hand without drawing new cards.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker, standing pat means keeping the hand dealt without swapping any, hence holding on to them.

clue.text: See 2
Across border current Wet struggling with Pellow finally having left (so a little bird told me)

definitions.text: so a little bird told me

indicators.note: across means straddling or spanning, so the river's letters stretch either side of the rest

parts.note: the River Tweed flows along the border between England and Scotland

indicators.note: struggling suggests floundering about, so the remaining letters are thrown into disorder
having left means these letters depart from the band's name

parts.note: Wet Wet Wet is a Scottish pop band

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of the singer's surname is used

explanation.surface: Marti Pellow of Wet Wet Wet has quit the band, or so rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: Marti Pellow fronted the Scottish pop band Wet Wet Wet. Take W (with) and W (Pellow's last letter) from WETWETWET under 'having left'; 'struggling' jumbles the rest to TTWEETE, which TWEED goes 'Across'.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdsong in the phrase 'a little bird told me' is the chirping by which the bird passed on its gossip.

clue.text: Dirty guy who returned to East End vice haunt

definitions.text: Dirty guy who returned to East End
definitions.meaning: Dirty ... Watts of the BBC soap EastEnders, set in London's East End, who returned after being presumed dead
a lair where crime or depravity goes on

explanation.definitionFit: Dirty Den was the villain of the British TV soap EastEnders, and a den of iniquity is a hideout for vice.

clue.text: See 14
Not being funny, sausage with top covered in chicken is coming up

indicators.note: being funny means acting oddly, so the letters of the short word are rearranged
in means the trimmed sausage goes inside the bird's letters

parts.note: a hen is a chicken

indicators.note: with its top covered up, the first letter of the sausage is hidden from view and lost

parts.note: chorizo is a spicy Spanish sausage

explanation.surface: Honestly, a sausage topped with chicken is on its way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being funny' turns NOT into ONT; 'with top covered' drops C from CHORIZO, and HORIZO goes 'in' HEN. 'Not being funny' reads as the idiom for 'seriously'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something approaching soon is said to be visible where sky meets land, an idiom for imminence.

clue.text: See 9
Stick a roundabout where traffic island should be?

indicators.note: where places one item at the spot named by the rest of the clue, here inside another

parts.note: a traffic island stands in a road, abbreviated RD
a roundabout is circular, like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone tells the council to build a roundabout instead of a traffic island.
explanation.walkthrough: A roundabout is shaped like O; put it in the middle of RD (road), where a traffic island would stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod is a thin straight stick or pole.

clue.text: See 6
See 1
Securing entry somehow, back Anfield fans to go up across country

indicators.note: securing means holding firmly, so the reversed fans' letters hold the others inside
back means the fans' letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the Kop is the famous stand of Liverpool supporters at Anfield

indicators.note: somehow suggests an unknown method, so the word entry is rearranged

explanation.surface: Liverpool fans getting tickets somehow travel cross-country to support the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the fans' stand, and 'Securing' holds the jumbled word inside it. 'up' means mounted, as on horseback; the Kop is Liverpool FC's home terrace at Anfield.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding small horses over open land is a holiday trek, and 'up' is the riding sense of being mounted.

clue.text: Something needed to muffle one Al Capone

parts.note: a scarf muffles the neck and face against the cold
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A gangster needed something to keep himself wrapped up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muffle' suggests silencing, as a gangster might, but means wrapping up warmly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chicago gangster was nicknamed for the knife wounds on his cheek.

clue.text: See 26
Greek king leads revolutionary bands against Italy

indicators.note: bands means wrapping round like a band, so the rearranged letters enclose the other pieces
revolutionary means overturning, so the letters of leads are turned into a new order

parts.note: on can mean against, as in leaning on a wall
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A Greek monarch heads rebel forces against Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads' looks like a verb with the king as subject, but it is the fodder for 'revolutionary', and 'bands' wraps it round the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spartan ruler who fell at Thermopylae was a famous monarch of ancient Greece.
